segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: One of the ways that we can celebrate God's presence with us is a practice called the love feast.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: It's something that the earliest communities of Christians would do when they gathered together, something that early Methodists also did when there wasn't a way for a preacher to be physically present, an ordained minister to be present to consecrate the sacrament of Holy Communion.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Families or friends, neighbors, church members would gather together and they would break bread.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: They would bring bread together and they would bring drink, often water or other drinks that they would have, and they would share together.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: As they had this meal, this love feast, they would share stories of how they'd seen God present in their lives and God's faithfulness in their lives.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
